title: BERT vs GPT-style Models
interviewAnswer: BERT-style models are typically encoder-only and learn bidirectional contextual representations; GPT-style models are decoder-only and autoregressively predict the next token. Their pretraining objectives drive different strengths.
why: BERT vs GPT tests whether you understand encoder-style bidirectional representation learning versus causal autoregressive generation.
intuition: BERT-style encoders can look both left and right to understand a token in context. GPT-style decoder-only models predict the next token using only earlier tokens.
deepDive: BERT is pretrained with masked-token objectives and is strong for embeddings/classification/extraction with task heads. GPT-style models use causal masks and next-token prediction, naturally supporting generation and in-context prompting. Modern systems blur categories with encoder-decoder and instruction-tuned variants, so choose based on task rather than brand.
workedExample: For semantic classification of a complete PR description, an encoder such as CodeBERT/BERT can produce contextual features. For generating an explanation, a causal LLM is more natural.
commonMistakes: Calling BERT generative in the same autoregressive sense as GPT.
Saying GPT has no bidirectional information at all—later tokens integrate all earlier context, but cannot see future tokens during causal prediction.
Assuming one family always has better embeddings.
followUps: How would you get sentence embeddings from BERT?
production: Encoder models are often cheaper for embeddings/classification; generative LLMs add latency/cost and should be used only when generation/reasoning is needed.
